content: The UCLA School of Public Health is a graduate-level institution dedicated to public health education and research. It is part of the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and is housed within the Center for Health Sciences building on the UCLA campus, located in the Westwood neighborhood of Los Angeles, California. The current Dean of the school is Dr. Linda Rosenstock, who holds both an MD and an MPH. The school boasts a network of over 8,000 alumni and employs more than 80 full-time faculty members. Its student body includes individuals from over 35 countries. History The University of California, Los Angeles began offering undergraduate courses in public health in 1946. For the following 15 years, public health education at UCLA was part of a broader University of California system-wide public health school. In 1957, UCLA initiated a program that allowed students to pursue advanced degrees in public health. The UCLA School of Public Health was officially established on March 17, 1961, with Lenor S. (Steve) Goerke serving as its inaugural dean. In 2003, the school expanded its offerings to include an undergraduate minor in public health. Departments and Degrees The UCLA School of Public Health provides graduate degrees across five primary departments: Biostatistics: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Community Health Sciences: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Environmental Health Sciences: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Epidemiology: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Health Services: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Additionally, the school offers two interdepartmental degrees: Environmental Science & Engineering: Doctor of Environmental Science and Engineering (DEnv). Molecular Toxicology: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The school also collaborates with other UCLA graduate programs to offer joint degrees, including: MPH/MA in African Studies MPH/MA in Asian American Studies MPH/MA in Islamic Studies MPH/MA in Latin American Studies MPH/JD with the School of Law MPH/MBA with the School of Management MPH/MD with the School of Medicine Research Centers The UCLA School of Public Health is affiliated with or sponsors several research centers, which focus on a wide range of public health issues. These include: The Center for Adolescent Health Promotion The Division of Cancer Prevention and Control Research The Center for Public Health and Disasters The Center for Environmental Genomics The Centers for Environmental Quality and Health The Center to Eliminate Health Disparities The Center for Healthier Children, Families, and Communities The UCLA Center for Health Policy Research The Center for Human Nutrition The Southern California Injury Prevention Research Center Notable Faculty The school has been home to many distinguished faculty members, including: Abdelmonem A. Afifi: Served as Dean of the School of Public Health from 1985 to 2000. Roslyn Alfin-Slater: Conducted groundbreaking research demonstrating that dietary cholesterol does not necessarily raise serum cholesterol levels. Lester Breslow: Served as Dean from 1972 to 1980 and was a former president of the American Public Health Association. E. Richard Brown: Also a former president of the American Public Health Association. Roger Detels: Served as Dean from 1980 to 1985 and conducted pioneering research on the transmission of HIV-related immune deficiency among homosexual men. Gladys Emerson: Played a key role in isolating and identifying the nutritional value of vitamin E. Jonathan Fielding: Currently serves as the Director of Public Health and Health Officer for Los Angeles County. Derek and Patrice Jelliffe: Advocated globally for the benefits of breastfeeding. Lenor S. (Steve) Goerke: The first Dean of the School of Public Health, serving from 1961 to 1972. Milton Roemer: Ruth Roemer: A former president of the American Public Health Association. Linda Rosenstock: The current Dean of the School of Public Health, serving since 2000. John Froines: A professor in environmental health sciences, former Director of Toxic Substances for the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), and a member of the Chicago Seven. Additionally, nine current faculty members are elected members of the prestigious National Academy of Medicine, a division of the National Academy of Sciences.
